title: Lyric Genie Docs
text: Lyric Genie Docs What everything in the app is, where it lives, and how the pieces connect. Lyric Genie is a songwriter's notepad. You write lyrics, you capture ideas by voice, and the app keeps the two attached to each other so a hummed melody and the verse it belongs to never drift apart. These docs are organised the way the app is: a page for each tab, a page for each kind of thing you make, and a page for every tool in the editor. Almost every question about Lyric Genie turns out to be a question about which thing something belongs to, which is why How it fits together is short and worth reading once. Your first song The short path, start to finish. How it fits together The five tabs, and what each one holds. The song editor Every control on the screen you write in. Collaboration Writing a song with someone else. FAQ Short answers to the usual questions. Troubleshooting When something is not behaving. Where to start # If you are new, Your first song walks the whole app in ten minutes. Then read How it fits together , which covers the one thing that trips most people up: a recording is not stored inside the tab you made it in. If you just want a quick answer, try the FAQ . If a

title: First launch
text: The first time you sign in, Lyric Genie asks you seven short questions before it lets you at the app. None of them takes longer than a tap, and two of them change how the app behaves afterwards. Step one of seven. The bar along the top is the whole wizard. The seven steps # Step What it asks What it does 1. Your name What should we call you? Becomes your display name , which is what co-writers see. Up to eighteen characters. 2. Role What best describes you? Songwriter, Artist, Producer or Hobbyist. Pick as many as fit. 3. Experience How much have you written? From Just Starting to Professional. 4. Where you found us How did you find us? Skippable, and the only step that is purely for us. 5. Voice Enable voice features The real iOS microphone and speech permissions. 6. Notifications Stay in the loop The real iOS notification permission. 7. In-line suggestions Enable In-line Suggestions A switch, on by default. The two that matter later # Voice. Microphone and speech recognition are system permissions, so this step hands you to iOS. Decline and Freestyle and recording cannot work at all. If you said no and changed your mind, it is in the iOS Settings app under Lyric Genie, not in Lyr

How it fits together
text: Lyric Genie has five tabs. Four of them hold a different kind of object, and the fifth is Settings. The bar along the bottom of every screen. Each one has a page of its own. Start with whichever tab you are standing in. Tab Holds What it is Start nothing of its own The launch pad. Jump straight into writing or recording. Songs Songs The documents you write lyrics in. Concepts Concepts Ideas you have not turned into songs yet. Recordings Recordings Every piece of audio you have captured, in one list. Settings — Account, plan, preferences. The rest of this page is the part the tab pages do not cover: how the things in them relate to each other. The one relationship that matters # A Recording belongs to a Song. Not to the Recordings tab. The Recordings tab is a view across all your audio, the way a photo library is a view across photos that also live in albums. When you record from inside a song, the audio is attached to that song and also appears in the Recordings list. When you record from the Start tab, there is no song yet, so the audio lands in the Recordings list unattached until you assign it. Note This is why the Recordings tab has an Add to Song action and the song editor doe

title: The Songs tab
text: The Songs tab is where your writing lives. It opens on All Songs , newest first, and that is the list most people never leave. 1 2 3 1 Sort and select, or start a song 2 Opening lines, so you can tell them apart 3 A shared song, marked Newest first. Tap a row to open it, press and hold for everything else. A row gives you the title, when you last touched it, and the opening lines, so you rarely have to open a song to know which one it is. A icon beside a title means that song is shared. If the song is filed in a project, a line above the title names it in that project's colour. A song in several projects lists them, and a song in none has no line at all. Inside a project the line only names the other projects a song is in, since the screen is already titled with this one. See Projects . The buttons along the top are a bell for notifications, a ⋯ for sorting and multi-select, and a compose button that starts a new song. Behind the back arrow # The ‹ beside the title is easy to miss, and it is the only way to the rest of the tab. It opens Collections , which is where All Songs itself lives alongside everything else your songs are filed in. 1 2 1 Two collections you always have 2 Fold

title: The Concepts tab
text: The Concepts tab holds ideas before they are songs. The app's own description is the clearest one: concepts are creative starting points that shape a song before you write a single word. They live here rather than in your song list so a half-formed idea does not sit alongside real work in progress. 1 2 1 Write one, or have them generated 2 Tap a card to open it out A card grid, newest first, with a search field for when it gets long. Each card is a title plus a mood, a theme and some similar artists. Tap one and it expands to show the whole thing, with a button to turn it into a song. The two buttons in the corner are the whole tab: + writes a concept by hand, and the sparkle generates a batch from songs you have already written. Where to go from here # Concepts for the fields, the generator and its switches, and what happens when a concept becomes a song. The song wizard for the other end of the same idea, which asks you three questions instead of proposing answers.

title: The Recordings tab
text: The Recordings tab is a view across all your audio. It is not where recordings are stored, which is the distinction that trips people up: a recording belongs to a song , and this tab lists them all regardless. 1 2 1 Filter, sort, and record a new one 2 The song it belongs to, and who made it One row per take. The song name on a row is the quickest way to tell an attached recording from a loose one. A row shows when it was made, how long it runs, the song it belongs to and the writer who made it. A recording with no song yet says Song Idea instead, and carries buttons for fixing that. Tap a row to expand it. You get playback, the transcript if there is one, and a ⋯ menu with export, rename, unlink, archive and delete. Where to go from here # Recordings for the object itself: attaching audio to a song, transcription, formats and storage. Recordings in a song for recording while you write, and for tying a take to particular lines. Freestyle for singing first and getting lyrics back. Note If you recorded something and cannot find it inside a song, it is almost certainly sitting here unattached. See How it fits together .

title: Songs
text: A song is the main document in Lyric Genie. It holds your lyrics, the context the writing tools read, any audio you attach, and, once it is shared, a tab for every writer on it. What a song holds # Part What it does Title Names the song everywhere it is listed. The editor can suggest one from your lyrics. Lyrics The main text, divided into sections by their headers. AI Context Mood, theme and similar artists. Every AI feature reads these. Scratchpad A private notepad that saves with the song but is not part of the lyrics. Recordings Audio attached to this song. See Recordings . Collaborator tabs One per writer on a shared song, plus Master. AI Context is the part people skip and then wonder why the suggestions are bland. It is three short fields, it takes a minute, and it changes the output of every AI feature in the app. The song wizard collects it by asking three questions. Finding one # The tab opens on All Songs , and the back arrow beside that title leads to the collections your songs are filed in. Both are covered on The Songs tab . Sorting and selecting # Inside a list, the ⋯ button sorts it and turns on multi-select. 1 2 3 1 Date created, last edited, or title 2 Turns on ch

title: What you can do to a song
Recordings
text: A recording is a piece of audio. You make one by recording in the app, or by importing a file you already have. Every recording either belongs to a song or does not yet. Both kinds appear in the Recordings tab, which is a list of all your audio regardless of where it came from. See The Recordings tab for that list and its controls. The two ways audio gets created # Recorded inside a song. Open a song, record, and the audio is attached to that song from the moment you stop. It also shows up in the Recordings tab. Recorded or imported on its own. Record from the Start tab, or import a file into the Recordings tab, and there is no song to attach it to yet. It sits in Recordings unattached. Recording from the Start tab. There is no song attached yet. Note Unattached is a normal state, not an error. Plenty of ideas arrive before the song they belong to exists. Telling the two apart # The label on a row is the fastest way to know which kind you are looking at. 1 2 1 No song yet 2 Two ways to give it one An unattached recording is labelled Song Idea and carries two buttons for fixing that. An unattached recording says Song Idea and offers New Song and Add to Song . Once it belongs to a so

Concepts
text: A concept is a song idea before it is a song. It holds a title, a mood, a theme and some similar artists. It does not hold lyrics, because an idea with lyrics is a song. The app's own description is the clearest one: concepts are creative starting points that shape a song before you write a single word. Concepts live in their own tab so a half-formed idea does not clutter your list of real work in progress. They are laid out as a grid of cards. See The Concepts tab . Writing one # Tap + on the Concepts tab and a blank card appears in place, with the four fields on it. 1 1 Only the title is required The placeholders are worth reading. They set the length these fields want. Only the title is required. Whatever you fill in carries across when the concept becomes a song, and lands in that song's AI Context. Letting the app write them # The sparkle button in the top right generates concepts from what you have already written. 1 2 3 1 Say what you are after, or leave it blank 2 What it reads to learn your taste 3 Four by default Leaving the description empty is fine. The switches do most of the work. Learn what I like from my existing songs is on by default, and it is what makes the resu

title: Projects
text: A project is a named folder of songs. An album, an artist you write for, a single co-writing session, a batch you are pitching. A project holds songs and nothing else. No lyrics of its own, no recordings, no concepts. Every song in a project is also in All Songs, because a project is a view of your songs rather than a place they move to. Making one # Open the Songs tab and tap New Project under the Projects heading, or the folder button in the top right. It asks for a name and a colour. 1 2 1 The name does most of the work 2 Seven, and one is already picked for you The same seven colours concepts use, so a folder and a card in the same colour match. The colour is the same set of seven that concepts use, and it is offered already picked: each new project is suggested the colour after the last one you made, so a row of projects varies without you choosing. Tap a different swatch if you have one in mind. There is no description field, so the name is still doing most of the work. "Winter EP" beats "New Project 2". What the colour does # It shows in two places. The folder icon on the Songs tab takes the colour, so you can pick a project out of a list of them without

title: The song wizard
text: Starting at a blank page is the hardest part. The song wizard asks three questions, then generates a title and some phrases so there is something on the page before you begin. Getting there # From the Start tab, tap Write and choose Guided Start . The other option, Blank Editor , skips all of this and opens an empty song. 1 2 1 Three questions, then ideas 2 Straight to an empty page Two ways to start, from the same button. The three questions # They are the same three fields as the AI Context bar in the song editor , asked one at a time. Whatever you answer is saved to the song, so filling them in here means not doing it later. Each step offers suggestion chips, and More reshuffles them if none fit. Skip moves past any question you would rather not answer. 1 2 1 Type your own, or pick from below 2 Suggestions, if nothing comes to mind The first of three, and you can pick up to three moods. Step What it is asking How many What's the mood? How the song should feel. Up to three. What's the theme? What happens in it, in a sentence. One. Similar Artists Who inspires the sound. Up to two. title: Freestyle
text: Freestyle records you and transcribes what you sang or said into editable lyrics. It is built for the moment where the melody arrives before the words do. Starting a Freestyle # There are two ways in, and they behave differently on purpose. From the Start tab. Tapping Freestyle starts recording immediately. You tapped the button because you had something to sing, and making you tap a second time loses the take. From inside a song. The microphone icon in the song editor opens Freestyle ready but not recording. You are already in a writing session, so the app waits for you. Tip If you want to set up before you sing, open a song and use the microphone icon rather than the Start tab. While you are recording # 1 2 3 1 The timecode counts recorded audio, not elapsed time 2 Undo takes back the last stretch you sang 3 Pause. The clock stops with it Freestyle part way through a take. The timecode counts the audio you have actually recorded. Pausing stops the clock, and resuming picks up where it left off, so the number always matches the length of the file rather than the time you spent with the screen open. Undo takes back the last segment , meaning everything since you last started or res

title: Importing files
text: Lyric Genie imports two different kinds of file: audio, which becomes a recording , and text, which becomes lyrics. There are two routes in. Pick a file from inside the app, or send something to Lyric Genie from another app's share sheet. Picking a file # The import button in the top bar of the Start tab takes either kind. The app works out what it got by inspecting the file itself, not by trusting the extension, so a mislabelled file still lands in the right place. Audio goes to Recordings. Text goes to lyrics. If you already know what you are importing, the tab menus are explicit. Where Menu item Takes Songs tab ⋯ Import Lyrics from File Text documents Recordings tab ⋯ Import Audio from File Audio files These two were both labelled "Import from Files" in older versions, which made them impossible to tell apart. They now say which is which. Sharing from another app # Lyric Genie appears in the iOS share sheet, which is the route most people actually use. It works from Voice Memos , Notes , Files , Mail , and anything else that shares audio or text. From Voice Memos: press and hold a memo, tap Share , and pick Lyric Genie. title: Sections and song structure
text: A section header is a line that names the part of the song underneath it. Lyric Genie picks them out, sets them in purple, and then uses them everywhere else. Naming your sections is optional, and it is the cheapest thing you can do to make the rest of the app work properly. Making one # Type the name of a section on its own line. That is the whole technique. 1 2 1 A header, set in purple automatically 2 Appears when your cursor is on a header line Headers are recognised as you type, not marked up by hand. Brackets are optional. The app strips them, so [Chorus] , (Chorus) , **Chorus** and plain Chorus all end up the same. Paste in lyrics from somewhere else and the headers usually survive the trip. Shorthand # You do not have to type the whole word. What you type What you get V1 , V2 Verse 1, Verse 2 PC , pre , prechorus , pre chorus Pre-Chorus HK Hook post , postchorus Post-Chorus Repeated sections are numbered for you as the song grows, so a second verse becomes Verse 2 without you counting. Changing a section's type # Put your cursor anywhere on a header and a button appears at the right of that line. Tap it to swap the section for another type. The current type carries a tick.

title: Wish Workshop
text: Wish Workshop is the main AI writing tool. You open it with the genie lamp button at the bottom right of the song editor . It does two quite different jobs, and which one you get depends entirely on whether you selected any text before you tapped the lamp. That is the single thing to understand about it. Two ways in # Select a line first and Wish Workshop works on that line. Your selection appears as a purple bubble at the top, the action button reads Replace , and a row of one-tap wishes lights up along the bottom. 1 2 3 1 The line you selected 2 Constraints. Both are on until you turn them off 3 One-tap wishes. Swipe for many more Selection mode. The workshop rewrites the line you gave it. Select nothing and you get Creative Spark instead, which generates new material rather than changing anything you wrote. The action button reads Insert , and the one-tap wishes are greyed out, because there is nothing for them to act on. Spark mode. The same sheet, a different job. It asks for context first # The first time you open it on a song with no AI Context , Wish Workshop stops and asks for some before it will do anything. Mood, theme and similar artists, asked for at the door. You can

title: Selecting and editing lines
text: Selecting text is how you point a tool at a particular line. Nothing in the editor works on your selection until you make one, and what the app offers back depends on how much you picked. Select a line and two things appear: a bar above the keyboard, and a menu on the selection itself. They hold different tools, so it is worth knowing which is which. The bar above the keyboard # Three buttons, and they are the ones you will reach for most. 1 2 3 1 Rhymes for the selected word 2 Synonyms and related words 3 Hands the line to Wish Workshop One line selected, so all three tools are available. Button What it does Available when Rhyme Opens the rhyme sheet for what you selected. The selection is one line or less. Thesaurus Opens synonyms and related words. The selection is one line or less. Rewrite Hands the selection to Wish Workshop to change. The selection is six lines or less. Those limits are why Rewrite reaches further than the other two. Rhyme and Thesaurus are word tools and need a phrase to work on. Rewrite is a writing tool, so it can take a whole stanza. Why the buttons go grey # They do not disappear when they are unavailable. title: Arrange mode
text: Arrange mode turns your lyrics into a checklist. Instead of a cursor and a keyboard you get a checkbox on every line, and a row of actions that move those lines around. It is for structure. Use it when the words are right but they are in the wrong order, or when a verse needs to become two. Getting in and out # The grid button at the bottom right of the editor opens it. The same button turns into a house, and tapping that takes you back to writing. 1 2 3 4 1 Tap a line to select it 2 Tap a section header and the whole stanza comes with it 3 The house takes you back to writing 4 The actions stay greyed until something is selected Arrange mode with two lines picked out of the first verse. Selecting # Tap any line to select it, and tap it again to let it go. The count in the middle of the bottom bar tells you how many you have. Press and drag down the column of checkboxes and every line you pass is selected. It is much faster than tapping a run of lines one at a time, and it is the fastest way to take a block that does not line up with a section. 1 1 Drag down this column Three lines in one gesture. Perform
text: Perform puts your lyrics on a black screen in large type and gets everything else out of the way. It is for the moment you stop writing and start singing. Open it from the ⋯ menu in the song editor . 1 2 1 Drag for bigger or smaller type 2 Close and go back to the editor Section headers stay grey so the shape of the song reads at a glance. What it changes # The screen goes black and stays dark whatever your phone is set to, because a bright screen in a dim room is the wrong thing to be looking at. Your lyrics are white, your section headers are grey. You can see where the chorus starts without reading the words. The edges fade rather than cutting off, so a line that is halfway on screen looks deliberate. Nothing is editable. You cannot change a word by accident with a microphone in your hand. The font size slider # The slider at the top runs between a small A and a large A . Drag it until the words are readable from wherever your phone is propped. Your choice sticks per song, so a song you have already set up opens the way you left it. Greyed out in the menu # Perform stays dimmed until the song has some lyrics. title: Rhymes
text: Most rhyming dictionaries take one word and give you words that rhyme with it. Lyric Genie takes your phrase, works out which syllables carry the rhyme, and then looks for words and phrases that match both of them. That is the difference worth understanding before you use it. It is built for internal and multisyllabic rhyme, not just the word at the end of the line. Opening it # Select a line or a word, then tap Rhyme in the bar above the keyboard. See Selecting and editing lines . The sheet works on one line or less. If Rhyme is greyed out, the selection is too big. 1 2 3 4 1 How many of the results the AI picked out for you 2 Slant loosens what counts as a rhyme 3 The syllables it is rhyming on. Tap one to move the anchor 4 Each tab is a different way of combining the two anchors The phrase "I love to sing", anchored on "love" and "sing". The anchors # Under your phrase is a row of chips, one per syllable, written the way they sound rather than the way they are spelled. In "I love to sing" they read eye · luhv · too · sing . Two of them are highlighted. Those are the anchors , the syllables the app thinks carry the rhyme. Everything else on

title: Looking up more than one word
Syllables
text: Sometimes a line says the right thing and does not fit the tune. It is a syllable short, or a syllable too long, and no amount of staring fixes it. The syllable tool rewrites the line to the length you need and keeps the meaning. Opening it # Select a single line, bring up the menu on the selection, and choose +1 Syllable or -1 Syllable . See Selecting and editing lines . Both only appear for a single-line selection, and -1 Syllable needs a line with at least two syllables to take one away from. 1 2 3 1 Tap the pencil to change the line without closing 2 Go two either way, not just one 3 How well it kept the meaning Asking for one more syllable on "I love to sing". Choosing how far to go # You arrive on the option you picked, and the four tabs let you change your mind without starting again. Tab What it does -2 Removes two syllables. -1 Removes one. +1 Adds one. +2 Adds two. Reading the results # Every suggestion carries two things. A score , which is how well the rewrite held on to your original meaning. It is coloured, so a green result kept the sense and a red one took liberties with it. High scores tend to be small additions like I love to sing out . Lower ones rearra

title: AI Style
text: AI Style is where you tell Lyric Genie how you want it to write, once, instead of saying it again in every wish. Everything here applies to the whole app rather than one song. Open it from the ⋯ menu in the song editor , or from Settings. 1 2 1 Free-form notes on how you want it to write 2 Words it will steer around Two settings, both of which the AI reads before it writes anything. Style Guidance # A free-form note about how you want suggestions written. Tone, perspective, the things you lean into, the things you are tired of. The app's own example is a good shape to copy: keep it conversational. no complex language. no weather metaphors. Short and blunt works better than a paragraph of theory. You have 300 characters, and the counter turns red as you reach the end. This is read by Wish Workshop and by in-line suggestions, so it shapes both the things you ask for and the things that appear on their own. Words to Avoid # A list of words you do not want to see. Type a word and it becomes a tag; tap the small cross on a tag to remove it. Songwriters tend to fill this with their own tics, or with the words that every AI reaches for. title: In-line suggestions
text: Stop typing for a moment and Lyric Genie offers a line where your cursor is. It sits there in purple, and it is not part of your song until you tap it. This is the one AI feature that comes to you rather than waiting to be asked. 1 2 3 1 Tap the line to take it 2 Or send it away 3 Swipe sideways for a different one A suggestion offered after a pause, still just an offer. What you can do with it # Action What happens Tap the suggestion It becomes part of your lyrics at the cursor. Swipe sideways Shows the next suggestion, when there is more than one. Tap the cross Dismisses it. Keep typing It disappears on its own. It also goes away if you move the cursor, leave the editor, or a co-writer edits the song. Nothing is inserted unless you tap. Turning it off # Preferences , from the ⋯ menu in the song editor or from Settings, has the switch. 1 1 The switch, under Song Editor In-line Suggestions is on by default for accounts with AI access. Plenty of writers turn it off. A suggestion that arrives while you are thinking is either helpful or an interruption, and which one depends entirely on how you work. title: What you can do with it
Lyric sheets
text: A lyric sheet is a web page of your finished lyrics with the writer credits underneath. You send someone a link and they read the song. No app, no account, no file to open. It is what you send a publisher, a co-writer's manager, or an artist you are pitching to. Making one # From the ⋯ menu in the song editor , choose Lyric Sheet . 1 2 3 1 Every sheet you have made for this song 2 Which words go on it, on a shared song 3 Who wrote it, and how they are credited Nothing is shared until you tap Create. What your reader sees # An ordinary web page. No app, no account, no file to open. A title, the writers, and the lyrics with their section headings. It reads on a phone or a laptop, and it is the same page whether you send it to a publisher or to a friend. Writer credits # You are added as a writer automatically, with your legal name filled in from your profile. Tap your name to open the rest of the fields. The details a publisher expects, filled in once and reused. Field What it is for Legal Name Your name as it appears on a split sheet, not your artist name. title: Inviting a co-writer
text: Collaboration in Lyric Genie works on invite codes. You generate one, your co-writer types it in, and the song appears in their app with both of you on it. Nothing is emailed. The screen is called Add Collaborator, so people expect an email to go out, and it does not. Note Collaboration is on the free plan. So are lyric sheets and recordings linked to lyrics. You do not need Pro to write with someone. Sending an invite # Open the song, tap Collaborators in the toolbar, then Add Collaborator . Before anyone is on the song. Pick + New Collaborator and confirm, and the app generates a code. 1 2 1 Six characters, good for one use 2 Or send the link instead One code, one collaborator, one use. Share Invite Link hands it to any messaging app you like. The code on its own works too, if you would rather read it down the phone. Each code can only be used once. Inviting two people means generating two codes. Joining a song # The person you invited goes to Settings , then Song Invite Code . Six characters, letters and numbers. Type the code, tap Join Song , and the song opens with both writers on it. It also lands in their Songs list from then on. When a code is refused # The person joining g

title: Collaborator tabs
text: Share a song and the editor grows a row of tabs. Each writer gets one, and everyone can see everyone else's. Nobody types over anybody. You write in your tab, they write in theirs, and the version you both agree on is assembled deliberately in a third one. 1 2 3 1 Your own tab, marked (You) 2 A co-writer. The star means they own the song 3 The agreed version Three tabs, three colours, one song. Reading the tabs # What you see What it means Your name (You) Your own tab. The only one you can type in. A star beside a name That writer owns the song. A filled dot They are in the song right now. An outlined dot They are not. Master The agreed version. See The Master . Colours are assigned, not chosen. The owner is purple and everyone else takes the next colour in the list, which is the same colour shown against their name on the Collaborators screen. What is yours and what is shared # Your tab is yours. Co-writers can read it but cannot edit it. To get your words into someone else's hands you send them, which is covered in Sending lines to a co-writer . Section headers take your colour. title: What is yours and what is shared
If you are removed, or you leave
Sending lines to a co-writer
text: Your tab is yours alone, so getting a line from your tab into a co-writer's means sending it. They decide whether to take it. That is the whole design. Nothing lands in anybody's lyrics without them agreeing to it. Sending # Open Arrange mode, the grid button at the bottom right, and select the lines you want. Tapping a section header takes the whole stanza. 1 2 1 Into the agreed version 2 Into a co-writer's mailbox A shared song adds two destinations to Arrange mode. Send to Collaborator asks who should get them. Pick a recipient, then Send. On someone else's tab the action changes to Send to Me , which pulls their lines into your own tab instead. Same idea, other direction. The mailbox # Lines you are sent wait in the mailbox, the button in the editor toolbar. It carries a count when something is waiting. 1 2 1 Received and Sent are separate lists 2 Read it before you decide Nothing is added to your tab until you accept it. Each card shows who sent it, which song it belongs to, when it arrived, and the lyrics themselves. Accept adds them to your tab. Decline turns them down, and the sender sees that it was declined. title: The Master
text: Master is the version of the song you both agree on. It is not anybody's personal tab, and it is not whatever the last person typed. Lines get put there on purpose. Every shared song has one, at the end of the tab row, in yellow. 1 1 Always last in the row The bridge was sent first. Master still puts the chorus above it. You cannot type in Master # This is the thing to understand before anything else. Master is not editable. Tap the words and nothing happens: no cursor, no keyboard. There is no lamp button on this tab either, so no Wish Workshop and no in-line suggestions. Everything in Master arrived from somebody's tab, and the only things you can do to it are reorder sections, delete them, or pull one back out. That is deliberate. If Master could be typed into, it would become a fourth draft competing with everyone else's, instead of the agreed version of the other three. To change a line, pull its section back to your own tab with Send to Me , edit it there, and send it again. Sending a section to Master # From your own tab, open Arrange mode, select what you want, and choose Send to Master . What happens next depends on what you selected. title: It files by section, not by arrival
Notifications
text: The bell on the Start tab collects everything that happened while you were not looking. A red dot means something is waiting. 1 2 1 What a co-writer did, and when 2 Grouped by kind, newest first Two real events from a shared song. What is in there # Notifications are grouped, and the groups appear in this order. Group What lands in it Invitations Someone asking you onto a song. Activity What your co-writers did. Reminders Nudges to pick a song back up. Offers Occasional offers on Pro. Collaboration events # Most of what you see comes from shared songs. Someone joined your song after accepting an invitation. A co-writer changed their lyrics . A co-writer sent you lines . See Sending lines to a co-writer . Someone changed the title , or the mood, theme and similar artists. A co-writer added a recording . A collaboration ended , because you were removed, you left, or the owner deleted their account. You keep a personal copy either way, and the message says so. Reminders # Two kinds arrive on their own. Keep writing. A song you left unfinished, usually with a suggestion attached, like adding a chorus or a bridge with Wish Workshop. Turn a recording into a song. A voice memo you capture

title: Signing in
text: Lyric Genie has two ways in: Continue with Google and Continue with Apple . That is the whole list. There is no email and password option, and no separate account to create. You pick one of the two and you are in. Note This surprises people who expect a sign-up form. There is not one, and you have not missed a step. Choosing Google or Apple the first time creates your account. Why it matters # Signing in is what makes your work sync. Your songs, recordings, concepts and projects live with your account, so they appear on any device you sign in on, and they survive reinstalling the app. If you are not signed in, you are not syncing. That is the single sentence worth remembering. Use the same one every time # Google and Apple are separate accounts as far as Lyric Genie is concerned. If you signed in with Google the first time and later tap Continue with Apple , you get a new, empty account rather than your songs. If your library looks empty on a device you have used before, that is almost always the reason. Sign out and back in with the other one. Tip If you cannot remember which you used, the answer is on the Settings tab. Your email address is under your name. When it will not work

title: Use the same one every time
Your profile
text: Your profile is two things at once: the name co-writers see, and the paperwork that goes on a lyric sheet. Open it by tapping your name at the top of Settings . 1 2 1 What co-writers see 2 What a publisher expects Fields save as you type. There is no Save button. Identity # Display Name is how you appear on a collaborator tab and in a co-writer's mailbox. Up to eighteen characters, with a counter under the field. This is your name, not your artist name, unless they are the same thing. Writer profile # These are the details a publisher, a PRO or a split sheet expects. Fill them in once and every lyric sheet you make starts with them already in place. Field What it is Legal Name Your full legal name, as it appears on a contract. Not your artist name. Writer IPI # Your Interested Party Information number, the identifier your PRO knows you by. Publisher Your publisher, if you have one. Publisher IPI # Their number. PRO Affiliation ASCAP, BMI, SESAC, SOCAN, PRS, APRA, or Other. PRO Name Only appears when you choose Other. Contact Email Where business enquiries should go. Tip Worth doing before you need it. title: Plans and Pro
text: Lyric Genie is free to use. Pro adds the AI writing tools and lifts the caps on rhymes and recording. The comparison as the app presents it. What Pro adds # Feature Free Pro In-line suggestions — Yes Wish Workshop — Yes Smart dictionaries — Yes AI song titles — Yes Song concepts and Spark — Yes Syllable control — Yes Rhyme lookups 30 a day Unlimited Voice recording 60 minutes in total Unlimited Longest single recording or import 5 minutes 60 minutes A dash does not mean locked. The free plan includes 7 of the larger AI calls and 40 of the lighter ones, so every AI feature above can be tried before paying. Pro is what makes them unlimited for the month. See Plan limits . What is free, and stays free # Three things people assume are paid, and are not. Collaboration . Inviting co-writers, tabs, sending lines, the Master tab. All of it. Lyric sheets . Making them and sharing them. Recordings linked to lyrics. Tying a take to particular words. Also free: writing, arranging, sections, Perform , importing, and the Scratchpad. Preferences
text: Preferences is the small set of switches that change how the app behaves for you. Reach it from Settings , or from the ⋯ menu inside the song editor . 1 2 3 1 Which tab the app opens on 2 Suggestions while you write 3 Lyrics in a serif face Four switches and one picker. App behaviour # Default Tab decides where the app opens: Start or Songs . Start is the launch pad, with the four big buttons and your latest songs. Songs is the full list. If you mostly return to work in progress rather than begin something new, Songs saves you a tap every time. Song editor # In-line Suggestions offers a line at your cursor after a pause. It has its own page, including what happens when you do not have AI access. See In-line suggestions . Serif Lyric Font sets your lyrics and titles in Academico, a serif face, instead of the default. The label itself is rendered in the serif so you can see what you are choosing before you choose it. Tip Worth trying even if you think you do not care. Some writers find a serif reads more like a page and less like a form, which changes how the words land. Communications # Two switches, both about email rather than the app. Switch What it sends Email Updates Tips, upda

title: Deleting your account
text: Delete Account & Data is at the very bottom of the Settings tab, below Sign Out, in red. It does what it says. This page exists so you know exactly what you are agreeing to before you tap it. Heads up Deleting your account is permanent. Your songs, recordings, concepts and projects are removed, and there is no undo and no grace period. If you only want to stop using the app on this device, sign out instead. What it asks you # The app checks three times, in three different ways, because the action cannot be taken back. 1 1 Tapping Yes here is not the end of it The first of three checks. Are you sure? The alert above, which says plainly that it is irreversible. Confirm deletion. A second alert warning that your song data will be unrecoverable. Prove it is you. A sign-in sheet, because deleting an account is not something a borrowed phone should be able to do. Only after all three does anything happen. Cancel is available at every step. While it runs # A full-screen progress view counts through the work: fetching your songs, deleting them one by one, cleaning up invitations, then your user data, then the account itself. It asks you not to close the app while this happens, and that

title: Plan limits
text: Every number on this page is generated from the app's own configuration when these docs are built, so it matches what the app actually enforces. Recording and audio # Free Pro Length of a single recording or import 5 minutes 60 minutes Total audio stored 60 minutes (1 hour) 10,000 minutes (about 167 hours) The per item cap applies to recording and to importing equally. A file you import cannot be longer than a recording you could have made. Writing tools # Free Pro Requests 7 total 5,000 per month Lighter requests are metered separately and more generously: 40 on free, 20,000 per month on Pro. The high-frequency features draw on this lighter pool, which is why they do not eat your main allowance: in-line suggestions and the rhyme sheet's AI picks . The two pools are not sealed off from each other. Once the lighter pool is used up, lighter requests start drawing on the main one instead, so the main number is the real ceiling. Your total across both is the two numbers added together, and never more. Rhyme lookups # Free Pro Lookups 30 per day Unlimited You are warned when you are down to your last 10 lookups for the day. Pro Pro plan Pro is a subscription, managed through your Apple

title: Supported formats
text: Audio # Format Extension Apple audio .m4a , .caf MP3 .mp3 WAV .wav AIFF .aiff , .aif AAC .aac , .mp4 FLAC .flac Everything is converted to M4A once it is in the app, on your device rather than on a server. Detection is based on the file's actual type rather than its name, so a file with a misleading extension is still routed correctly. Lyrics and text # Format Extension Plain text .txt Rich text .rtf Markdown .md PDF .pdf Word document .docx Note PDFs are read for their text. A PDF that is a scan of a page, with no text layer, will come in empty. Sharing into the app # Lyric Genie appears in the iOS share sheet for both audio and text, so a voice memo or a note can be sent to it directly rather than exported and imported. Every format on this page works that way, and so does plain shared text with no file behind it at all. See Importing files for what happens next. Size limits # Kind Limit Audio By length, not size. 5 minutes free, 60 minutes on Pro. Text 5 MB

title: Glossary
text: Lyric Genie names a few things in ways that are not obvious from the outside. This is what each one means. What you make # Song The document you write lyrics in. It holds the lyrics themselves, a title, an AI Context, a Scratchpad, any recordings you attach, and on a shared song a tab per writer. See Songs . Concept An idea that is not a song yet: a title, a mood, a theme, and optionally some similar artists. Concepts sit upstream of songs and can become one when you are ready. See Concepts . Recording A piece of audio. A recording belongs to a song, or to nothing yet. Either way it appears in the Recordings tab. See Recordings . Project A named, colour-tagged folder that holds a list of songs. The colour shows on the folder and above the title of every song in it. An album, an artist you write for, a session. See Projects . Inside a song # AI Context Three fields attached to the song: mood, theme, and similar artists. Everything the AI writes for that song is steered by them. The song wizard collects them by asking you three questions. See The song editor . Scratchpad A ruled notepad that slides up from the bottom of the editor. It saves with the song but is not part of your lyric

title: FAQ
text: Answers here are deliberately short. Each one links to the page that goes into it properly. Does it write songs for me # No, and it will not try. Every AI feature in Lyric Genie works on material you have already given it: a line to rewrite, a song with a mood and a theme attached, a phrase to find rhymes for. There is no button that produces a finished song from nothing. The closest thing is Creative Spark, which writes new material for a song that already has an AI Context. See Wish Workshop . Do I need Pro # Not to write, not to record, and not to collaborate . The free plan gives you unlimited songs, 60 minutes of recordings, 30 rhyme lookups a day, and 7 of the larger AI calls. Pro raises those limits and adds Refine Context and in-line suggestions. See Plans and Pro and Plan limits . Can my co-writer use the free plan # Yes. Collaboration is free on both sides. There is no difference between what a free co-writer and a Pro co-writer can do on a shared song. Do I have to sign in # Yes, and it is what makes syncing work. Your songs and recordings live in your account, so the same library appears on every device you sign in on. Sign-in is Google or Apple. There is no email and p

Troubleshooting
text: Most of what looks like a bug in Lyric Genie is a control that is waiting for something. This page is grouped by where the problem shows up. Where did my work go # I signed in and my library is empty # You are almost certainly in the other account. Lyric Genie signs in with Google or with Apple, and those are two separate accounts even when both use the same email address. Songs written under one are invisible to the other. Sign out, sign back in with the other button, and check whether your songs are there. Nothing has been deleted. I recorded something and cannot find it in my song # Open the Recordings tab. If the recording was made from the Start tab rather than from inside a song, it is unattached and waiting there. Use Add to Song on it. This is the most common confusion in the app and it is worth reading How it fits together once to get the shape of it. My lyric sheet does not show the changes I made # A lyric sheet is a frozen snapshot , taken at the moment you created it. Editing the song afterwards never changes a link you have already sent, which is the point: what you sent a publisher last week still reads the way it did when you sent it. Make a new sheet when you want
